claim: PFG (PBANKA0902300) is a target gene of AP2-G.
source: We screened for novel sequence-specific TFs among target genes that were functionally unannotated in PlasmoDB (https://plasmodb.org/plasmo/app/) using highly conserved amino acid sequences among Plasmodium species as a criterion.
evidence: The text states PFG was identified through screening of AP2-G target genes, and Figure 1E shows ChIP-seq data demonstrating AP2-G binding upstream of PFG.

claim: PFG encodes a 2709 amino acid protein with two highly conserved regions among Plasmodium species.
source: Through this screening, a gene encoding a 2709 amino acid protein with two regions highly conserved among Plasmodium was identified (PBANKA0902300, designated as a partner of AP2-FG [PFG]; Figure 1A).
evidence: Direct statement in text with supporting schematic diagram in Figure 1A showing the protein structure.

claim: The two conserved regions of PFG comprise 108 and 139 amino acids, respectively.
source: The two conserved regions comprised 108- and 139 amino acids, respectively, and each region showed 94 and 91% conservation between P. berghei and Plasmodium falciparum (Figure 1B).
evidence: Specific amino acid counts and conservation percentages are provided with alignment data in Figure 1B.

claim: PFG regions show 94% and 91% conservation between P. berghei and P. falciparum.
source: The two conserved regions comprised 108- and 139 amino acids, respectively, and each region showed 94 and 91% conservation between P. berghei and Plasmodium falciparum (Figure 1B).
evidence: Conservation percentages are explicitly stated and supported by alignment data in Figure 1B.

claim: Genes homologous to PFG exist broadly among apicomplexan parasites and in alveolates closely related to Apicomplexa, such as Vitrella brassicaformis.
source: The Blastp search (https://blast.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/Blast.cgi) using these regions revealed that genes homologous to PFG exist broadly among apicomplexan parasites and also in alveolates closely related to Apicomplexa, such as Vitrella brassicaformis (Figure 1C; Oborník et al., 2012), whereas a large inter-region between these two regions present in all Plasmodium homologs was not observed in these proteins (Figure 1A).
evidence: Blastp search results are described with citation and supported by phylogenetic data in Figure 1C.

claim: PFG is expressed only in female gametocytes and the protein is localized in the nucleus.
source: Fluorescence analysis showed that this gene is expressed only in female gametocytes and the protein is localized in the nucleus (Figure 1D), suggesting its involvement in the transcriptional regulation of female gametocytes.
evidence: Fluorescence microscopy data in Figure 1D shows GFP signal in female gametocytes with nuclear localization.

claim: PFG is specifically transcribed in female gametocytes according to sex-specific transcriptome data.
source: According to sex-specific transcriptome data (Witmer et al., 2020), the PFG is specifically transcribed in female gametocytes.
evidence: Statement is supported by citation to published transcriptome data.

claim: PFG harbors AP2-FG peaks with binding motifs in the upstream region.
source: We examined the target genes of the female-specific transcriptional activator AP2-FG and found that PFG had been predicted as a target of AP2-FG and harbored AP2-FG peaks with binding motifs in the upstream region (Figure 1E).
evidence: ChIP-seq data in Figure 1E shows AP2-FG binding peaks upstream of PFG with identified motifs.

claim: PFG expression becomes visible from 20 hpi (hours post-infection).
source: Temporal profiling of the expression of PFG using PFG::GFP parasites showed that the expression became visible from 20 hpi (Figure 1F).
evidence: Time-course fluorescence microscopy data in Figure 1F shows GFP signal appearing at 20 hpi.

claim: The timing of PFG expression is approximately 4 hours later than that of AP2-FG, which starts at 16 hpi.
source: The timing of the expression was approximately 4 hr later than that of AP2-FG, which started at 16 hpi (Yuda et al., 2019).
evidence: Comparison of expression timing with cited reference for AP2-FG expression.

claim: The asexual stages of PFG(-) parasites proliferated as wild-types.
source: The asexual stages of PFG(-) parasites proliferated as wild-types (Figure 2A), and morphologically mature male and female gametocytes were observed on Giemsa-stained blood smears (Figure 2B).
evidence: Parasitemia data in Figure 2A shows no difference between wild-type and PFG(-) parasites.

claim: Morphologically mature male and female gametocytes were observed in PFG(-) parasites on Giemsa-stained blood smears.
source: The asexual stages of PFG(-) parasites proliferated as wild-types (Figure 2A), and morphologically mature male and female gametocytes were observed on Giemsa-stained blood smears (Figure 2B).
evidence: Microscopy images in Figure 2B show mature gametocyte morphology in PFG(-) parasites.

claim: No oocysts were observed on the mosquito midgut wall 14 days after infective blood meal in two independent PFG(-) clones.
source: However, in mosquito transmission experiments, no oocysts were observed on the mosquito midgut wall 14 d after the infective blood meal in two independent clones (Figure 2C).
evidence: Oocyst count data in Figure 2C shows zero oocysts for PFG(-) parasites compared to wild-type.

claim: Only approximately 20% of the female gametocytes in PFG(-) parasites were converted into zygotes in ookinete cultures.
source: In ookinete cultures, only approximately 20% of the female gametocytes were converted into zygotes, and no banana-shaped or retort-form ookinetes were generated (Figure 2D).
evidence: Ookinete culture data in Figure 2D shows conversion rates for PFG(-) parasites.

claim: No banana-shaped or retort-form ookinetes were generated in PFG(-) parasites.
source: In ookinete cultures, only approximately 20% of the female gametocytes were converted into zygotes, and no banana-shaped or retort-form ookinetes were generated (Figure 2D).
evidence: Ookinete culture data in Figure 2D shows absence of mature ookinete forms in PFG(-) parasites.

claim: Ookinetes were formed when PFG(-) parasites were crossed with normal females (P48/45(-)) but not when crossed with normal males (P47(-)).
source: In the cross-fertilization experiment, ookinetes were formed when crossing with normal females (P48/45(-)) but not when crossing with normal males (P47(-)), demonstrating that the abnormal phenotype observed in PFG(-) was indeed derived from female gametocytes (Figure 2E).
evidence: Cross-fertilization data in Figure 2E shows ookinete formation only when PFG(-) provides males.

claim: The abnormal phenotype observed in PFG(-) was derived from female gametocytes.
source: In the cross-fertilization experiment, ookinetes were formed when crossing with normal females (P48/45(-)) but not when crossing with normal males (P47(-)), demonstrating that the abnormal phenotype observed in PFG(-) was indeed derived from female gametocytes (Figure 2E).
evidence: Cross-fertilization experiment results demonstrate the female-specific defect.

claim: No RFP-positive parasites were detected in PFG(-)820 parasites by FACS analysis.
source: Although female gametocytes with mature morphology were observed on Giemsa-stained blood smears as the original 820 parasites, in fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS) analysis, no RFP-positive parasites were detected in the PFG(-)820 parasites (Figure 2F).
evidence: FACS data in Figure 2F shows absence of RFP signal in PFG(-)820 parasites.

claim: GFP-positive parasites were observed in PFG(-)820 parasites as in the original 820 parasites.
source: In contrast, GFP-positive parasites were observed in them as in the original 820 parasites (Figure 2F).
evidence: FACS data in Figure 2F shows GFP signal present in PFG(-)820 parasites.

claim: The promoter activity of the female-specific CCP2 gene was severely reduced by the disruption of PFG.
source: These results indicated that the promoter activity of the female-specific CCP2 gene used for RFP expression in 820 parasites was severely reduced by the disruption of PFG.
evidence: Inference from FACS data showing loss of RFP expression driven by CCP2 promoter.

claim: 279 genes were significantly downregulated in PFG(-) parasites (log2(fold change) < –2 and adjusted p-value <0.001).
source: In PFG(-) parasites, 279 genes were significantly downregulated (log2(fold change) < –2 and p-value adjusted for multiple testing with the Benjamini–Hochberg procedure <0.001), more than 90% of which were female-specific genes according to sex-specific transcriptome data (Witmer et al., 2020; Figure 2G).
evidence: RNA-seq analysis results shown in volcano plot in Figure 2G.

claim: More than 90% of the significantly downregulated genes in PFG(-) parasites were female-specific genes.
source: In PFG(-) parasites, 279 genes were significantly downregulated (log2(fold change) < –2 and p-value adjusted for multiple testing with the Benjamini–Hochberg procedure <0.001), more than 90% of which were female-specific genes according to sex-specific transcriptome data (Witmer et al., 2020; Figure 2G).
evidence: RNA-seq data analysis with reference to published sex-specific transcriptome data, shown in Figure 2G.

claim: Transcripts of the CCP2 gene decreased over 20 times in PFG(-) parasites.
source: Consistent with the results of the gene targeting experiment in 820 parasites, transcripts of the CCP2 gene decreased over 20 times in PFG(-)parasites.
evidence: RNA-seq data showing fold change in CCP2 expression.

claim: Genes significantly downregulated in PFG(-) constituted more than half of the female-enriched genes (258/504).
source: Genes significantly downregulated in PFG(-) constituted more than half of the female-enriched genes (258/504, Supplementary file 1), suggesting that the expression of female-specific genes was globally downregulated in PFG(-) parasites.
evidence: RNA-seq data analysis comparing downregulated genes to known female-enriched genes.

claim: 1073 and 1204 peaks were identified in the genome in ChIP-seq experiments 1 and 2 of PFG, respectively.
source: In two biologically independent experiments, experiments 1 and 2, 1073 and 1204 peaks were identified in the genome, respectively (Supplementary file 2a and b), and 95% (1029 peaks) of the peaks identified in experiment 1 were common with those identified in experiment 2 (Figure 3A).
evidence: ChIP-seq peak calling results shown in Figure 3A and supplementary files.

claim: 95% (1029 peaks) of the peaks identified in ChIP-seq experiment 1 of PFG were common with those identified in experiment 2.
source: In two biologically independent experiments, experiments 1 and 2, 1073 and 1204 peaks were identified in the genome, respectively (Supplementary file 2a and b), and 95% (1029 peaks) of the peaks identified in experiment 1 were common with those identified in experiment 2 (Figure 3A).
evidence: ChIP-seq reproducibility analysis shown in Venn diagram in Figure 3A.

claim: PFG ChIP-seq peaks were observed upstream of genes significantly downregulated in PFG(-) parasites.
source: These peaks were observed upstream of the genes significantly downregulated in PFG(-) parasites, suggesting that PFG is directly involved in the transcriptional activation of these genes (examples of graphic images are shown in Figure 3B).
evidence: ChIP-seq peak locations shown in IGV images in Figure 3B for downregulated genes.

claim: Binding of PFG to the genome was associated with ten-base motif sequences, TGTRNNYACA.
source: Statistical analysis of genomic sequences around the summits of peaks (common peaks, the same hereafter) showed that binding of PFG to the genome was associated with ten-base motif sequences, TGTRNNYACA (Figure 3C), the female-specific cis-acting element identified in the ChIP-seq of AP2-FG (Yuda et al., 2019).
evidence: Motif enrichment analysis shown in sequence logo in Figure 3C.

claim: The ten-base motif TGTRNNYACA is the female-specific cis-acting element identified in the ChIP-seq of AP2-FG.
source: Statistical analysis of genomic sequences around the summits of peaks (common peaks, the same hereafter) showed that binding of PFG to the genome was associated with ten-base motif sequences, TGTRNNYACA (Figure 3C), the female-specific cis-acting element identified in the ChIP-seq of AP2-FG (Yuda et al., 2019).
evidence: Reference to previously published ChIP-seq data for AP2-FG.

claim: The peaks identified in the ChIP-seq of PFG were co-localized with those of AP2-FG.
source: In comparison with the graphical views, the peaks identified in the ChIP-seq of PFG were co-localized with those of AP2-FG (Figure 3B).
evidence: IGV images in Figure 3B show overlapping peaks for PFG and AP2-FG.

claim: The position of PFG peaks was consistent with the ChIP-seq peaks of AP2-FG throughout the genome.
source: An heat map positioned at the peak summit of PFG in the center showed that the position of the peaks was consistent with the ChIP-seq peaks of AP2-FG throughout the genome (Figure 3D).
evidence: Heat map analysis in Figure 3D shows genome-wide co-localization of PFG and AP2-FG peaks.

claim: PFG and AP2-FG form a complex on the ten-base motif and cooperatively activate their targets.
source: These results strongly suggest that these two TFs form a complex on the ten-base motif and cooperatively activate their targets.
evidence: Inference from co-localization of ChIP-seq peaks and shared binding motif.

claim: Some of the AP2-FG peaks lacked the corresponding ChIP-seq peaks of PFG.
source: On the other hand, graphic images also showed that some of the AP2-FG peaks lacked the corresponding ChIP-seq peaks of PFG (Figure 3E).
evidence: IGV images in Figure 3E show AP2-FG peaks without corresponding PFG peaks.

claim: 1077 and 881 peaks were obtained in ChIP-seq of PFG using PFG::GFPAP2-FG(-) parasites, with 847 peaks common between them.
source: ChIP-seq of PFG in PFG::GFP parasites with the AP2-FG gene disrupted (PFG::GFPAP2-FG(-)), 1077 and 881 peaks were obtained, and 847 peaks were common between them (Figure 4A and Supplementary file 2c and d).
evidence: ChIP-seq peak calling results shown in Venn diagram in Figure 4A.

claim: PFG peaks in PFG::GFPAP2-FG(-) parasites showed no apparent changes compared to those obtained for the original PFG::GFP parasites.
source: These peaks showed no apparent changes compared to those obtained for the original PFG::GFP parasites (Figure 4B).
evidence: IGV images in Figure 4B show similar peak patterns between conditions.

claim: The positions of PFG peaks obtained in PFG::GFPAP2-FG(-) parasites were consistent with those obtained for PFG::GFP parasites throughout the genome.
source: The heat map showed that the positions of PFG peaks obtained in PFG::GFPAP2-FG(-) parasites (common peaks, the same hereafter) were consistent with those obtained for PFG::GFP parasites throughout the genome, and vice versa (Figure 4C).
evidence: Heat map analysis in Figure 4C shows genome-wide consistency of peak positions.

claim: The same ten-base motif obtained in the PFG::GFP parasites was enriched around the summits of the PFG peak obtained in PFG::GFPAP2-FG(-) parasites.
source: Statistical analysis showed that the same ten-base motif obtained in the PFG::GFP parasites was enriched around the summits of the PFG peak obtained in PFG::GFPAP2-FG(-) parasites (Figure 4D).
evidence: Motif enrichment analysis shown in sequence logo in Figure 4D.

claim: PFG binds to the ten-base motif even in the absence of AP2-FG.
source: These results indicate that PFG binds to the ten-base motif even in the absence of AP2-FG.
evidence: Inference from ChIP-seq data showing PFG binding to ten-base motif in AP2-FG(-) parasites.

claim: 575 and 492 peaks were obtained in ChIP-seq of AP2-FG using AP2-FG::GFPPFG(-) parasites, with 457 peaks common between them.
source: ChIP-seq of AP2-FG obtained in AP2-FG::GFP parasites with the PFG gene disrupted (AP2-FG::GFPPFG(-)), 575 and 492 peaks were obtained, and 457 peaks were common between them (Figure 4E and Supplementary file 2e and f).
evidence: ChIP-seq peak calling results shown in Venn diagram in Figure 4E.

claim: Upon disruption of PFG, AP2-FG peaks common with PFG peaks disappeared, and only AP2-FG peaks not common with PFG peaks remained.
source: Comparison with PFG peaks showed that upon disruption of PFG, AP2-FG peaks common with PFG peaks disappeared, and only AP2-FG peaks not common with PFG peaks remained (Figure 4F).
evidence: IGV images in Figure 4F show loss of co-localized peaks in PFG(-) background.

claim: The ten-base motif disappeared and two distinct motifs, GCTCA and TGCACA, became the most enriched motifs around the summits of AP2-FG peaks in PFG(-) parasites.
source: In line with this, statistical analysis showed that the ten-base motif disappeared and instead two distinct motifs, GCTCA and TGCACA, became the most enriched motifs around the summits of these peaks (common peaks, the same hereafter) with a p-value of 2.1 × 10–27 and 1.3 × 10–28, respectively (Figure 4G).
evidence: Motif enrichment analysis shown in sequence logos in Figure 4G.

claim: PFG is essential for binding AP2-FG to the ten-base motif.
source: These results suggest that PFG is essential for binding AP2-FG to the ten-base motif, that is, PFG mediates AP-FG binding to the ten-base motif.
evidence: Inference from loss of ten-base motif enrichment in AP2-FG ChIP-seq when PFG is disrupted.

claim: AP2-FG binds to the genome in two distinct forms, with and without PFG.
source: The results also suggest that AP2-FG binds to the genome in two distinct forms, with and without PFG, and that the former form binds to the ten-base motif, TGTRNNYACA, and the latter binds to other motifs, supposedly GCTCA or TGCACA.
evidence: Inference from different motif enrichment patterns in ChIP-seq with and without PFG.

claim: The form of AP2-FG with PFG binds to the ten-base motif, TGTRNNYACA.
source: The results also suggest that AP2-FG binds to the genome in two distinct forms, with and without PFG, and that the former form binds to the ten-base motif, TGTRNNYACA, and the latter binds to other motifs, supposedly GCTCA or TGCACA.
evidence: Inference from ChIP-seq data showing ten-base motif enrichment when both proteins are present.

claim: The form of AP2-FG without PFG binds to motifs GCTCA or TGCACA.
source: The results also suggest that AP2-FG binds to the genome in two distinct forms, with and without PFG, and that the former form binds to the ten-base motif, TGTRNNYACA, and the latter binds to other motifs, supposedly GCTCA or TGCACA.
evidence: Inference from ChIP-seq data showing GCTCA and TGCACA motif enrichment in PFG(-) background.

claim: Introducing three-point mutations into the ten-base motif upstream of PBANKA_1346300 reduced the %input value to background levels in ChIP-qPCR.
source: Three-point mutations were introduced into the motif using the CRISPR/Cas9 system, and GFP was fused to the PFG gene in these parasites (Figure 4H). Introducing these mutations reduced the %input value to background levels (Figure 4I), demonstrating that the motif is essential for PFG binding to the genome.
evidence: ChIP-qPCR data in Figure 4I shows loss of PFG binding when motif is mutated.

claim: The ten-base motif is essential for PFG binding to the genome.
source: Introducing these mutations reduced the %input value to background levels (Figure 4I), demonstrating that the motif is essential for PFG binding to the genome.
evidence: ChIP-qPCR experiment with motif mutation demonstrates requirement for binding.

claim: The five-base motif sequence GCTCA was highly enriched around the summits of DIP-seq peaks with a p-value of 2.6 × 10–246.
source: Around the summits of the peaks obtained by DIP-seq analysis, the five-base motif sequence GCTCA, identical to one of motifs enriched around the summits of ChIP-seq peaks described above, was highly enriched with a p-value of 2.6 × 10–246 (Figure 5A).
evidence: DIP-seq motif enrichment analysis shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Two motifs, GATCA and ACTCA, which may be variants of the GCTCA motif, were enriched in DIP-seq with p-values of 2.0 × 10–153 and 6.8 × 10–51, respectively.
source: In addition, two motifs, GATCA and ACTCA, which may be variants of the GCTCA motif, were also enriched, with p-value of 2.0 × 10–153 and 6.8 × 10–51, respectively (Figure 5A).
evidence: DIP-seq motif enrichment analysis shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The six-base motif, TGCACA, was not enriched around DIP-seq peaks (p-value=0.051).
source: In contrast, the six-base motif, TGCACA, was not enriched around DIP-seq peaks (p-value=0.051), suggesting that it is not a binding motif of AP2-FG.
evidence: Statistical analysis of DIP-seq data shows lack of enrichment for TGCACA motif.

claim: 84.2% of the sAP2-FG ChIP-seq peaks contained at least one of the five-base motifs within 300 bp from the summits.
source: In the ChIP-seq of sAP2-FG, 84.2% of the peaks contained at least one of these five-base motifs within 300 bp from the summits, and the average distance from the summits was 62.4 bp (Figure 5B).
evidence: Analysis of motif distribution relative to ChIP-seq peaks shown in histogram in Figure 5B.

claim: The average distance from the summits to the five-base motifs was 62.4 bp in sAP2-FG ChIP-seq peaks.
source: In the ChIP-seq of sAP2-FG, 84.2% of the peaks contained at least one of these five-base motifs within 300 bp from the summits, and the average distance from the summits was 62.4 bp (Figure 5B).
evidence: Analysis of motif distribution relative to ChIP-seq peaks shown in histogram in Figure 5B.

claim: The most enriched motif matched well with the binding sequence of the AP2 domain of P. falciparum AP2-FG reported by Campbell et al., 2010.
source: The most enriched motif matched well with the binding sequence of the AP2 domain of P. falciparum AP2-FG, which was reported by Campbell et al., 2010.
evidence: Comparison with previously published binding motif data.

claim: AP2-FG binds directly to the five-base motifs through its AP2 domain.
source: Collectively, these results suggested that AP2-FG binds directly to these motifs through its AP2 domain.
evidence: Inference from DIP-seq using recombinant AP2 domain showing direct DNA binding.

claim: Introducing mutations to the five-base motif upstream of NEK2 decreased AP2-FG association with the locus to background levels.
source: We prepared parasites with this motif mutated from AP2-FG::GFPPFG(-) parasites (Figure 5C) and performed a qPCR assay with anti-GFP antibodies. Upon addition of the mutation, the AP2-FG associated with the locus decreased to background levels (Figure 5D).
evidence: ChIP-qPCR data in Figure 5D shows loss of AP2-FG binding when five-base motif is mutated.

claim: The five-base motif is essential for the binding of sAP2-FG to the upstream of target genes.
source: A ChIP-qPCR assay was performed to confirm that this motif is essential for the binding of sAP2-FG to the upstream of target genes.
evidence: ChIP-qPCR experiment with motif mutation demonstrates requirement for binding.

claim: Promoter activity was reduced by introducing mutations to the ten-base motifs in the P28 promoter.
source: Promoter activity was reduced by introducing mutations to the ten-base motifs, but the signals were still retained.
evidence: FACS analysis of reporter expression with mutated motifs.

claim: Signals became almost undetectable by introducing mutations into the five-base motifs in the P28 promoter.
source: The signals became almost undetectable by introducing mutations into the five-base motifs.
evidence: FACS analysis of reporter expression with mutated motifs.

claim: The five-base motifs are female-specific cis-acting elements and function independently of the ten-base motif in the promoter.
source: These results demonstrate that the five-base motifs are female-specific cis-acting elements and function independently of the ten-base motif in the promoter.
evidence: Promoter assay results showing independent function of five-base motifs.

claim: 810 genes were predicted as targets of cAP2-FG from ChIP-seq peaks of PFG.
source: As targets of cAP2-FG, 810 genes were predicted from ChIP-seq peaks of PFG obtained from PFG::GFP parasites (common peaks of two experiments, the same hereafter) (Figure 6A and Supplementary file 3a).
evidence: Target prediction from ChIP-seq peak locations relative to genes.

claim: 321 genes were predicted as target genes for sAP2-FG by ChIP-seq in AP2-FG::GFPPFG(-) parasites.
source: As target genes for sAP2-FG, 321 were predicted by ChIP-seq in AP2-FG::GFPPFG(-) parasites (Figure 6B and Supplementary file 3b).
evidence: Target prediction from ChIP-seq peak locations relative to genes.

claim: 967 genes were identified as targets for either cAP2-FG or sAP2-FG, and 164 genes were common between them.
source: As a result of these target predictions, 967 genes were identified as targets for either cAP2-FG or sAP2-FG, and 164 genes were common between them (Figure 6C).
evidence: Venn diagram analysis in Figure 6C showing overlap of target gene sets.

claim: PFG is a target of sAP2-FG and cAP2-FG.
source: Target prediction also showed that PFG is a target of sAP2-FG and cAP2-FG.
evidence: ChIP-seq peaks for both forms of AP2-FG found upstream of PFG.

claim: Upstream of PFG harbors the binding sites of three different TFs: AP2-G, sAP2-FG (AP2-FG), and cAP2-FG (PFG).
source: Upstream of PFG harbors the binding sites of three different TFs: AP2-G, sAP2-FG (AP2-FG), and cAP2-FG (PFG) (Figure 6D).
evidence: IGV images in Figure 6D show ChIP-seq peaks for all three TFs upstream of PFG.

claim: PFG is activated in early females by sAP2-FG and then by cAP2-FG in later female gametocytes.
source: These results suggest that PFG is activated in early females by sAP2-FG and then by cAP2-FG in later female gametocytes.
evidence: Inference from presence of both sAP2-FG and cAP2-FG binding sites upstream of PFG and expression timing.

claim: The zygote TF AP2-Z was predicted to be a target of cAP2-FG only.
source: Meanwhile, the zygote TF AP2-Z was predicted to be a target of cAP2-FG only (Nishi et al., 2022).
evidence: Target prediction from ChIP-seq data with citation to previous work.

claim: Among the 279 genes significantly downregulated in PFG(-) parasites, 165 genes were targets for PFG (unique for PFG or common for sAP2-FG and PFG).
source: Among the 279 genes significantly downregulated in PFG(-) parasites, 165 genes were targets for PFG (unique for PFG or common for sAP2-FG and PFG), and only 4 genes were targets unique to sAP2-FG.
evidence: Integration of RNA-seq and ChIP-seq data to identify direct targets affected by PFG disruption.

claim: Only 4 genes among the significantly downregulated genes in PFG(-) parasites were targets unique to sAP2-FG.
source: Among the 279 genes significantly downregulated in PFG(-) parasites, 165 genes were targets for PFG (unique for PFG or common for sAP2-FG and PFG), and only 4 genes were targets unique to sAP2-FG.
evidence: Integration of RNA-seq and ChIP-seq data to identify direct targets affected by PFG disruption.

claim: The average log2(fold change) value was significantly higher (less downregulated) in targets unique to sAP2-FG than in targets unique to cAP2-FG (p=1.3 × 10–10) or common targets (p=1.4 × 10–5).
source: The log2 distribution (fold change = PFG(-)/wild type) in the three groups of target genes showed that the average value was significantly higher (i.e., less downregulated) in targets unique to sAP2-FG than in the other two groups (targets unique to cAP2-FG or common targets for both), with p-values of 1.3 × 10–10 and 1.4 × 10–5, respectively, by two-tailed Student's t-test (Figure 6F).
evidence: Statistical analysis of RNA-seq fold changes shown in box plots in Figure 6F.

claim: The trans-activity of cAP2-FG and sAP2-FG is independent of each other.
source: These results suggest that the trans-activity of cAP2-FG and sAP2-FG is independent of each other.
evidence: Inference from differential impact of PFG disruption on different target gene classes.

claim: The binding of AP2-FG to the ten-base motif is mediated by another female-specific TF, PFG.
source: In this study, we report two findings that change our previous view. First, the binding of AP2-FG to the ten-base motif is mediated by another female-specific TF, PFG.
evidence: Summary statement based on ChIP-seq experiments showing loss of AP2-FG binding to ten-base motif in PFG(-) parasites.

claim: There is another cis-acting element in female-specific promoters, and AP2-FG binds to this element directly as a trans-activating factor.
source: Second, there is another cis-acting element in female-specific promoters, and AP2-FG binds to this element directly as a trans-activating factor.
evidence: Summary statement based on identification of five-base motif through ChIP-seq and DIP-seq experiments.

claim: PFG is upregulated in two steps in female gametocytes; first by sAP2-FG, and then by cAP2-FG.
source: This study suggests that PFG is upregulated in two steps in female gametocytes; first by sAP2-FG, and then by cAP2-FG.
evidence: Inference from presence of both sAP2-FG and cAP2-FG binding sites upstream of PFG.

claim: Transcriptional activation of PFG by cAP2-FG constitutes a transcriptional positive feedback loop.
source: Transcriptional activation of PFG by cAP2-FG constitutes a transcriptional positive feedback loop, suggesting that after activation by sAP2-FG, PFG maintains its transcription through this autoactivation mechanism.
evidence: Inference from PFG being a target of cAP2-FG, which requires PFG for its binding.

claim: After activation by sAP2-FG, PFG maintains its transcription through an autoactivation mechanism.
source: Transcriptional activation of PFG by cAP2-FG constitutes a transcriptional positive feedback loop, suggesting that after activation by sAP2-FG, PFG maintains its transcription through this autoactivation mechanism.
evidence: Inference from positive feedback loop mechanism.

claim: As the expression of PFG increases via the autoactivation mechanism, AP2-FG recruited by PFG (cAP2-FG) increases and eventually becomes predominant in the transcriptional regulation of female gametocytes.
source: As the expression of PFG increases via this mechanism, AP2-FG recruited by PFG (cAP2-FG) increases and eventually becomes predominant in the transcriptional regulation of female gametocytes.
evidence: Inference from positive feedback mechanism and target gene analysis.

claim: Expression of many unique targets of PFG decreases in AP2-FG-disrupted parasites.
source: This is supported by the observation that expression of many unique targets of PFG decreases in AP2-FG-disrupted parasites (Yuda et al., 2019).
evidence: Reference to previously published RNA-seq data from AP2-FG(-) parasites.

claim: In AP2-FG-disrupted parasites, while female gametocytes display immature morphologies, a few develop into retort-form ookinetes.
source: In AP2-FG-disrupted parasites, while female gametocytes display immature morphologies, a few develop into retort-form ookinetes.
evidence: Reference to previously published phenotypic characterization of AP2-FG(-) parasites.

claim: RFP signals in female gametocytes could still be detected in AP2-FG(-)820 parasites by FACS even though RFP signals were reduced to undetectable level in PFG(-)820 parasites.
source: The observation also supports this assumption that RFP signals in female gametocytes could still be detected in AP2-FG(-)820 parasites by FACS (Yuda et al., 2019) even though RFP signals were reduced to undetectable level in PFG(-)820 parasites under the same experimental conditions.
evidence: Comparison of FACS data from current study with previously published data.

claim: The promoter of the CCP2 gene is still active in AP2-FG(-)820 parasites.
source: This suggests that the promoter of the CCP2 gene, which is a target of PFG only, is still active in AP2-FG(-)820 parasites.
evidence: Inference from detection of RFP signal driven by CCP2 promoter in AP2-FG(-) parasites.

claim: PFG continues to activate its transcription through a positive feedback loop once it is induced by AP2-G and complements the absence of AP2-FG.
source: It is assumed that PFG continues to activate its transcription through a positive feedback loop once it is induced by AP2-G and complements the absence of AP2-FG.
evidence: Inference from continued PFG expression in AP2-FG(-) parasites and autoactivation mechanism.

claim: PFG(-) parasites completely lose their ability to develop into ookinetes because the expression of genes necessary for ookinete development is significantly reduced.
source: PFG(-) parasites completely lose their ability to develop into ookinetes because the expression of genes necessary for ookinete development is significantly reduced.
evidence: Integration of phenotypic data (no ookinetes) with RNA-seq data (downregulation of ookinete genes).

claim: PFG(-) parasites manifest mature morphologies in females owing to the induction of the genes necessary for female development by sAP2-FG.
source: However, they manifest mature morphologies in females owing to the induction of the genes necessary for female development by sAP2-FG.
evidence: Inference from phenotypic observation and understanding of sAP2-FG function.

claim: AP2-FG(-) parasites show immature morphologies in females because the expression of genes involved in female development is downregulated in the early stage.
source: In contrast, AP2-FG(-) parasites show immature morphologies in females because the expression of genes involved in female development is downregulated in the early stage.
evidence: Inference from phenotypic observation and understanding that sAP2-FG is lost in AP2-FG(-) parasites.

claim: AP2-FG(-) parasites retain the ability to fertilize and develop into retort-form ookinetes because PFG is still expressed in AP2-FG(-) and activates genes for zygote/ookinete development.
source: Despite this immature morphology, they retain the ability to fertilize and develop into retort-form ookinetes because PFG is still expressed in AP2-FG(-) and activates genes for zygote/ookinete development.
evidence: Inference from phenotypic observation and understanding of PFG function.

claim: P. falciparum gametocytes require 9–12 days to mature, which is much longer than that of P. berghei.
source: P. falciparum gametocytes require 9–12 d to mature, which is much longer than that of P. berghei (Gautret and Motard, 1999).
evidence: Statement supported by citation to published literature.

claim: The ten-base motif is highly enriched in the upstream regions of gametocyte-specific genes in P. falciparum.
source: Meanwhile, it has been reported that the ten-base motif is highly enriched in the upstream regions of gametocyte-specific genes also in P. falciparum (Young et al., 2005).
evidence: Statement supported by citation to published literature.

claim: PFG is likely to play an important role in the transcriptional regulation of female gametocyte development in P. falciparum.
source: Thus, despite the difference in maturation periods, PFG is likely to play an important role in the transcriptional regulation of female gametocyte development in P. falciparum.
evidence: Inference from conservation of ten-base motif in P. falciparum and PFG's role in P. berghei.

claim: The two forms of AP2-FG correspond to distinct female-specific cis-acting elements and play pivotal roles in female gametocyte development.
source: In conclusion, our results suggest that the two forms of AP2-FG, which correspond to distinct female-specific cis-acting elements, play pivotal roles in female gametocyte development and can generate variations among female-specific promoters.
evidence: Summary inference from all experimental data showing two binding modes and their functions.

claim: The two forms of AP2-FG can generate variations among female-specific promoters.
source: In conclusion, our results suggest that the two forms of AP2-FG, which correspond to distinct female-specific cis-acting elements, play pivotal roles in female gametocyte development and can generate variations among female-specific promoters.
evidence: Inference from identification of two distinct binding modes with different target preferences.

claim: AP2-G is essential for gametocyte generation.
source: AP2-G is essential (Sinha et al., 2014). Disruption of this gene causes the parasite to lose its ability to generate gametocytes.
evidence: Statement supported by citation to published literature.

claim: In P. berghei, AP2-G expression starts from the late trophozoite at 14–16 hpi and peaks at 18 hpi when sexual stage-specific features first appear.
source: In P. berghei, its expression starts from the late trophozoite at 14–16 hpi and peaks at 18 hpi when sexual stage-specific features first appear (Yuda et al., 2021).
evidence: Statement supported by citation to published literature.

claim: P. berghei AP2-G induces hundreds of genes that contain several TFs important for the development of gametocytes.
source: P. berghei AP2-G induces hundreds of genes that contain several TFs important for the development of gametocytes, suggesting that induction of these TFs by AP2-G generates a driving force for gametocytogenesis (Yuda et al., 2021).
evidence: Statement supported by citation to published literature.

claim: AP2-FG is a target gene of AP2-G.
source: AP2-FG is a member of the Plasmodium AP2 family of TFs and is a target genes of AP2-G (Yuda et al., 2021; Yuda et al., 2019).
evidence: Statement supported by citations to published literature.

claim: AP2-FG is a female-specific TF and plays an essential role in the development of female gametocytes.
source: AP2-FG is a female-specific TF and plays an essential role in the development of female gametocytes.
evidence: Statement based on established knowledge from previous studies.

claim: In P. berghei, AP2-FG is expressed from early gametocytes to mature females.
source: In P. berghei, AP2-FG is expressed from early gametocytes to mature females, and by disruption of AP2-FG, the development of the female gametocytes is impaired, showing immature morphologies and resulting in complete loss of capability to mediate parasite transmission to mosquitoes.
evidence: Statement based on established knowledge from previous studies.

claim: By disruption of AP2-FG, the development of the female gametocytes is impaired, showing immature morphologies and resulting in complete loss of capability to mediate parasite transmission to mosquitoes.
source: In P. berghei, AP2-FG is expressed from early gametocytes to mature females, and by disruption of AP2-FG, the development of the female gametocytes is impaired, showing immature morphologies and resulting in complete loss of capability to mediate parasite transmission to mosquitoes.
evidence: Statement based on established knowledge from previous studies.

claim: AP2-FG binds to a ten-base female-specific cis-acting element and regulates variety of genes including those for fertilization, meiosis, and the development of ookinetes.
source: This TF binds to a ten-base female-specific cis-acting element and regulates variety of genes including those for fertilization, meiosis, and the development of ookinetes.
evidence: Statement based on established knowledge from previous studies.

claim: AP2-FG-disrupted parasites can produce ookinetes with decreased numbers and abnormal morphologies.
source: However, AP2-FG-disrupted parasites can produce ookinetes with decreased numbers and abnormal morphologies, suggesting that additional mechanisms for activating female-specific genes are still functional upon the disruption of AP2-FG.
evidence: Statement based on established knowledge from previous studies.

claim: Additional mechanisms for activating female-specific genes are still functional upon the disruption of AP2-FG.

evidence: Inference from phenotypic observation of AP2-FG(-) parasites.

claim: In P. berghei, early gametocytes manifest morphologies distinguishable from asexual stages at 18 hpi.
source: In Plasmodium berghei, early gametocytes manifest morphologies distinguishable from asexual stages at 18 hpi (hours post-infection of the new red blood cell) and manifest sex-specific features at 20 hpi.
evidence: Statement supported by citation to published literature.

claim: In P. berghei, early gametocytes manifest sex-specific features at 20 hpi.
source: In Plasmodium berghei, early gametocytes manifest morphologies distinguishable from asexual stages at 18 hpi (hours post-infection of the new red blood cell) and manifest sex-specific features at 20 hpi.
evidence: Statement supported by citation to published literature.

claim: In P. berghei, gametocytes complete a sex-specific maturation process at approximately 24–26 hpi.
source: They then complete a sex-specific maturation process, during which a sex-specific gene expression repertoire is established, at approximately 24–26 hpi (Mons et al., 1985).
evidence: Statement supported by citation to published literature.

claim: In females, genes necessary for fertilization and protein synthesis are expressed.
source: In females, genes necessary for fertilization and protein synthesis are expressed, and the number of transcripts is stored in an untranslated state in the cytoplasm to prepare for zygote development (Mair et al., 2006; Guerreiro et al., 2014).
evidence: Statement supported by citations to published literature.

claim: In female gametocytes, transcripts are stored in an untranslated state in the cytoplasm to prepare for zygote development.

evidence: Statement supported by citations to published literature.

claim: In males, genes for flagella-based motility and genome replication are expressed, as well as genes for fertilization.
source: In males, genes for flagella-based motility and genome replication are expressed, as well as genes for fertilization.
evidence: Statement based on established knowledge of male gametocyte biology.
